title: AI Unlocked: Law & Legal Practice
blurb: For lawyers, paralegals, and compliance teams: research and drafting acceleration, contract review workflows, the legal-AI tool market compared, and the professional-responsibility rules (competence, confidentiality, candor) that make or break adoption.

modules.d: Where AI transforms practice — and the sanctions that teach caution.
modules.body:
Landscape

  • Research, first-draft contracts, discovery review, and client intake are being transformed; judgment, advocacy, and counsel are not.
  • The cautionary canon: lawyers sanctioned for filing AI-hallucinated citations — competence now includes verifying AI output.
  • Bar guidance worldwide converges on three duties: competence with the tools, confidentiality of client data, candor about what AI produced.
Cathy O’Neil’s Weapons of Math Destruction showed how algorithms become "opinions embedded in code" — nowhere more consequential than in justice. Even the U.S. Chief Justice’s 2023 year-end report conceded AI will transform legal work while insisting human judgment remains the core of judging. Both truths shape every module here.

modules.d: Memos, contracts, and correspondence — verification built in.
modules.body:
Workflows

  • Issue-spotting and research plans drafted; every authority Shepardized/verified by you.
  • Contract first drafts from your precedent bank; clause-by-clause explanation for clients at plain-language level.
  • Correspondence and demand letters at three assertiveness levels; deposition/hearing prep question banks.
  • Devil's advocate: opposing counsel simulation on your own argument before filing.
plAIbox™: produce a research memo with a verification log showing how each cited authority was confirmed.
🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as a research associate (I remain responsible for all verification). For this legal question in [jurisdiction]: [describe], produce an issue-spotting memo: questions presented, the analytical framework, the categories of authority I must pull, opposing arguments I should anticipate, and a verification checklist for every authority before use.

modules.t: Tool Study: The Legal AI Market
modules.d: Harvey/CoCounsel-class vs Spellbook-class vs general LLMs — access and economics.
modules.body:
Comparative snapshot

  • Enterprise legal AI (Harvey, Thomson Reuters CoCounsel-class): research + drafting grounded in legal databases; firm-level procurement, premium pricing; strongest citation reliability.
  • Contract-focused tools (Spellbook-class, in-Word assistants): per-seat subscriptions accessible to small firms; live inside your drafting environment.
  • General LLMs (Claude/ChatGPT): most flexible and affordable; NO authoritative legal database — treat every legal assertion as unverified.
  • Selection: matter types × jurisdiction coverage × confidentiality terms (DPA, training-use opt-out) × budget per fee-earner.

modules.d: Review pipelines, playbooks, and obligation tracking.
modules.body:
Workflows

  • Review playbooks: your firm's positions encoded so AI flags deviations, you decide.
  • Batch NDA/vendor review with risk-ranked summaries (our SMB contract-review methodology, professionalized).
  • Obligation extraction into compliance calendars; regulatory-change monitoring digests.

modules.d: Client data rules, privilege risks, and disclosure norms.
modules.body:
Hard lines

  • Client-identifying data only in tools with contractual confidentiality (DPA/enterprise terms, training opt-out) — consumer chatbots are presumptively off-limits for privileged material.
  • Privilege: prompts and outputs may be discoverable — write accordingly.
  • Client disclosure and billing honesty for AI-accelerated work; court AI-disclosure standing orders checked per forum.

quiz.q: Privileged client material may be processed…
opts: Only in tools with contractual confidentiality protections

modules.body:
Capstone

  • Two live workflows with verification logs, your tool matrix with confidentiality terms, and a one-page Practice AI Protocol (approved tools, data rules, verification standard, disclosure norm) — presented to the panel as if to your managing partner.
